paper: step 8. Provisional Section 3.3. The commons reference evaluation model is a trained artifact.
adr: Diagnostic checkpoint sweep. Same corpus, taxonomy, and gate as the training recipe. Training base is SmolLM3-3B after a measured 0.6B capacity ceiling. This run does not decide the published pin; it samples the loss curve so a sweet spot or a capacity ceiling is a measured fact. The live pin is unchanged.

base.note: Read at run time from the manifest. repoId here is a pin that must match. This is the training base. Do not change the live evaluator pin in this diagnostic.

framework.whyNotUnsloth: 3B plus 3936 short examples on an 80GB card does not need Unsloth's memory path. The standard stack is the one a reader can follow without a third training runtime. SmolLM3 modeling code requires transformers >= 4.53.0; the pin below is that version or newer.
framework.torch: supplied by the GPU image; not pinned here so a CUDA wheel is not overwritten

train.evalDatasetNote: The held-out suite is the final gate, never a training or hyperparameter split. The sweep gates after the fact. It does not train against the suite.

sweep.purpose: First SmolLM3-3B run. Sample the training curve the same way the 0.6B ceiling was measured. One GPU run, many gated checkpoints. Not a second gate, not a label change, not a live-pin swap.

llamaCpp.note: convert_hf_to_gguf.py then llama-quantize Q8_0. The run records the resolved commit in checkpoints.json.

time.estimate: Training three epochs of 3B LoRA is tens of minutes on an 80GB card. Six merge-plus-Q8_0 exports of 3B and six 187-item CPU gates dominate the wall time. If the train loop itself is still running after 90 minutes, stop and report.
